info.title: Mock Server runtime-control API
info.summary: Drive a running mock server — flip scenarios, manage profiles, reset sequence progress, and read request logs.
info.description:
The JSON HTTP API behind the mock server's dashboard, served under `/ui/api/*`.

Mock endpoints answer at the root (`/…`), so the control API cannot live there without colliding with a mocked route; `/ui` is the reserved admin namespace.

**Local-dev only.** The API is unauthenticated (matching the dashboard) and gives no isolation guarantees — global mocks are a single shared switch that parallel callers can clobber. Use profiles for per-caller isolation. It does not author mocks; you create endpoints and fixtures by writing catalog files.

**Versioning.** `info.version` is this contract's own version, independent of the server build (which `GET /ui/api/health` reports as `version` and `sha`). The contract evolves additively: new routes, new optional request fields, new response fields, and new enum members can appear in any release, so ignore fields you do not recognise. Error bodies are `{ "error": string, "code": string }` — the envelope is stable and `code` is safe to match on; the `error` message text is not.

servers.description: The running mock server, which serves this document at /ui/api/openapi.json.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: Read-only discovery of the systems, endpoints, and scenarios the server loaded at startup.

tags.name: Global mocks
tags.description: The single shared scenario switch used by `mockType: "global"` endpoints.

tags.name: Profiles
tags.description: Per-caller scenario selections, keyed by a business ID such as `customer-123`.

tags.name: Logs
tags.description: What the server recorded for each handled request.

get.description: Returns the checked-in contract for every `/ui/api/*` route, as served by this build.

get.summary: List systems, endpoints, and declared scenarios
get.description: Read-only projection of the loaded catalog: systems → endpoints → declared scenarios. Carries no fixture bodies.

Backs the dashboard's scenario-preview modal: it returns the fixture body or resolver source for a single declared scenario, already syntax-highlighted. The implicit `real` passthrough has no file and is not declared, so it answers `404` here.

The `html` fields are presentation data for the dashboard. Scripts should read `json` or `code`.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: A scenario key declared on the endpoint.

404.description: No such system/endpoint (`code: "unknown_endpoint"`), or the endpoint declares no such scenario (`code: "unknown_scenario"`).

get.summary: List the global scenario overrides in force
get.description: Returns one record per endpoint with a global override set, most recently changed first. Endpoints left on their implicit default are absent.

put.summary: Set the global scenario for an endpoint
put.description:
The endpoint must be `mockType: "global"`, and the scenario must be selectable on it — any declared scenario (fixture- or resolver-backed) or the implicit `real` passthrough.

The endpoint is resolved before the body is read, so an unknown system/endpoint answers `404` even when the body is malformed.

400.description: The endpoint is not a global mock (`code: "endpoint_not_global"`), the body is not valid JSON (`invalid_json`), `scenario` is missing or empty (`scenario_required`), or the scenario is not declared on the endpoint (`scenario_not_declared`).

delete.description: Reverts the endpoint to its implicit default and drops the endpoint's resolver history. Idempotent — clearing an override that was never set still answers `204`.

404.description: No profile with that ID. `code` is `"profile_not_found"`.

put.description:
`endpointScenarios` is replaced wholesale, so omitting it — or sending `{}` — clears every selection on the profile. Each key is validated against the catalog, and the write is all-or-nothing: one unknown endpoint name or undeclared scenario rejects the whole request.

Selections are normalised on the way in: a selection equal to the implicit scenario is dropped, a one-step sequence collapses to a plain string, and an empty sequence is dropped. The response is the stored profile, exactly as `GET` would return it.

A successful write also records a `profile_saved` admin entry in the request log.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON (`code: "invalid_json"`); or `endpointScenarios` is not an object, an endpoint name is unknown, a selection is neither a string nor an array of strings, or a scenario is not declared on its endpoint (`code: "invalid_scenario_selection"` for all four — see `error` for which one).

delete.summary: Delete a profile and everything keyed to it
delete.description: Cascades to the profile's key mappings, sequence progress, resolver history, and request logs. Idempotent — deleting a profile that does not exist still answers `204`.

204.description: The profile and its dependent data are gone.

post.description: Clears sequence progress and resolver history so the next call starts from the first step. With an `endpoint`, only that endpoint resets; with no body — or a malformed one — the whole profile resets. Always answers `204`, and records a `progress_reset` admin entry in the request log.

get.description:
Newest first, ordered by timestamp then log ID. Summaries omit the captured request and response bodies by default — fetch one entry by ID for those, or send `include=full` to get them inline on every row instead. Every filter is optional and they combine with AND.

Sending `minCount` or `waitMs` turns the call into a bounded wait: the request is held open until that many entries match, then answers with `matched` saying whether the threshold was reached. It is meant for awaiting calls in tests without a client-side polling loop.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Keep only entries for this profile ID.

parameters.name: endpoint
parameters.description: Keep only entries for this endpoint name.

parameters.name: errorsOnly
parameters.description: Send `1` to keep only entries whose outcome is `error`. Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: validation
parameters.description: Keep only entries whose schema check landed in this state on either side of the exchange. `issues` is the union of `failed` and `drift`; `ok` means something was checked and nothing was wrong; `unchecked` means no check ran. An unrecognised value is ignored rather than rejected, so a bad filter never fails the request.

parameters.name: logId
parameters.description: Case-insensitive prefix match on the log ID — paste an `x-mock-log-id` response header straight in.

parameters.name: traceId
parameters.description: Keep only entries with this exact distributed-trace ID (32 lowercase hex from `traceparent`, or an `x-request-id` verbatim — see `LogEntryCommon.traceId`). Exact match, unlike `logId`'s prefix search.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: keep only entries newer than this log ID. An unknown ID is ignored.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Keyset cursor: keep only entries older than this log ID. Takes precedence over `since` if both are sent; an unknown ID yields an empty page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, clamped to 1–200. A missing or unparseable value falls back to 100.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Send `full` to return each entry's full payload — the captured request and response bodies included — instead of the lighter summary projection. Any other value is ignored.

parameters.name: minCount
parameters.description: Hold the request open until at least this many entries match the filters, then answer. Pair it with `since` to count only entries newer than a cursor — that is how you await "this endpoint has been called N more times" in one request instead of a polling loop. Sending it without `waitMs` waits the default window; values below 1, and unparseable ones, are treated as 1. The threshold is counted over all matching entries, so it is independent of `limit` — read `matched` rather than `entries.length` to learn whether it was reached.

parameters.name: waitMs
parameters.description: How long to wait for `minCount`, in milliseconds, clamped to 0–60000. Sending it without `minCount` waits for a single matching entry. Unparseable values fall back to 10000, the default applied when `minCount` is sent alone. The request answers as soon as the threshold is reached, and always by the deadline; `0` checks once and returns. A `before` page never waits — its match count cannot grow.

200.description: The matching entries, newest first. Each is a `LogSummary` by default, or a full `LogEntry` when the request set `include=full`.

entries.description: `LogSummary` by default; `LogEntry` (carrying `request`/`response` payloads) when the request set `include=full`. Every entry in a given response shares the same shape. `anyOf` rather than `oneOf`: `LogSummary` places no constraint on `request`, so a full `LogEntry` also validates against it.

matched.description: Whether the `minCount` threshold was reached before `waitMs` ran out. Present only when the request asked to wait (it sent `minCount` or `waitMs`); absent on an ordinary listing. `false` still carries whatever matched, so a timed-out wait is a normal `200` with a partial page, not an error.

get.description:
Returns the decision trace plus the captured request and response.

`bodyHtml` is presentation data for the dashboard — syntax-highlighted markup for the same bodies. Scripts should read `entry` and ignore it. A side is omitted when that body is absent or was stored as a raw string rather than structured JSON, and the whole field is omitted when neither side qualifies, so treat every level as optional. Nothing is available only as markup.

parameters.name: logId
parameters.description: The full log ID, as carried by the `x-mock-log-id` response header.

200.description: The entry, and the dashboard's markup for its bodies.

404.description: No entry with that ID — it may have aged out of the log's TTL window. `code` is `"log_not_found"`.

get.description: Pings MongoDB with a 3-second bound, so an unreachable database answers promptly instead of hanging on the driver's 30-second server-selection timeout. Both outcomes also report the running build, which makes this the endpoint to poll when waiting for the server to come up in CI.

200.description: The server is up and MongoDB answered the ping.

503.description: MongoDB did not answer within the check's window. Carries the same fields as `200`, plus `error`.

SystemSlug.name: system
SystemSlug.description: A system slug, as returned by `GET /ui/api/catalog`.

EndpointName.name: endpoint
EndpointName.description: An endpoint name within the system, as returned by `GET /ui/api/catalog`.

ProfileId.name: profileId
ProfileId.description: The caller's business ID, such as a customer or account number. Profiles are created on first write — there is no separate registration step.

Error.title: Error
Error.description: The body of every non-2xx JSON response except `GET /ui/api/health`'s `503` (see `HealthUnavailable`). The envelope is stable and both fields are always present; `error` is human-readable and may change wording between releases, so match on `code`, not on `error`.

error.description: Why the request failed, for humans. Wording may change between releases.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable identifier for the failure. Safe to match on. The current values are `invalid_json`, `unknown_endpoint`, `unknown_scenario`, `endpoint_not_global`, `scenario_required`, `scenario_not_declared`, `invalid_scenario_selection`, `profile_not_found`, and `log_not_found` — see the response description on the operation that returned this body for which ones apply there. Not modelled as an enum: new values can be added in additive releases, so treat one you don't recognise as a generic failure rather than rejecting the response.

Catalog.title: Catalog
Catalog.description: The catalog the server loaded at startup. It is read once, so it only changes across restarts.

slug.description: URL-safe system identifier, taken from the directory name under `catalog/`. Use it in the `{system}` path segments.

baseUrlEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the real upstream base URL that the `real` passthrough scenario proxies to.

name.description: Endpoint identifier, unique across the whole catalog. This is the key a profile's `endpointScenarios` maps, and the `{endpoint}` path segment.

method.description: HTTP method the mocked endpoint answers.

path.description: Path the mocked endpoint is served at, relative to the server root.

mockType.description: Where the served scenario comes from: `profiled` reads the caller's profile, `global` reads the single shared switch. Always present — an endpoint that omits it in the catalog is projected as `profiled`.

profileIdSelector.description: How the engine resolves this endpoint's caller into a profile ID. Present on every `profiled` endpoint (the catalog fails to load without one) and absent on every `global` endpoint (the catalog fails to load if one is declared there) — so this field and `mockType` always agree. Exposed exactly as authored, so a client can show or replicate it verbatim: `$.<path>` reads parsed JSON body (`$.customer.customerId`, `$.items[0].id`), `path:<name>` a path parameter, `query:<name>` a query-string parameter, `header:<name>` a request header (matched case-insensitively), `bearer` the raw `Authorization: Bearer` credential, `bearer:<claim>` a top-level claim decoded from that credential as a JWT, and `profileKey:<namespace>:<selector>` resolves a key captured by an earlier request's `captureProfileKeys` instead of reading the ID directly.

captureProfileKeys.description: Extra request keys this endpoint captures and links to its resolved profile ID, on top of resolving that ID itself — so a later, unrelated request can be routed to the same profile via `profileIdSelector: "profileKey:<namespace>:<selector>"`. Only a profiled endpoint whose own `profileIdSelector` resolves the ID directly (not itself a `profileKey:…` lookup) may declare captures. Present only when the endpoint's catalog definition includes this field; omitted, not an empty array, when the field itself is absent.

namespace.description: The captured mapping's namespace, matching `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*`. A later endpoint reads it back via `profileKey:<namespace>:<selector>`.

keySelector.description: Where in this request the value to capture is read from. Uses the same direct-selector grammar as `profileIdSelector` (`$.…`, `path:`, `query:`, `header:`) except `bearer`, which is profile-ID-only.

resolverScenarios.description: The subset of `scenarios` keys backed by a `<slug>.mjs` resolver rather than a `<slug>.json` fixture. Always present, and empty when the endpoint has none.

scenarios.description: Every declared scenario as slug → label, fixture- and resolver-backed alike. The `real` passthrough is implicit on every endpoint and never appears here.

ScenarioView.title: ScenarioView
ScenarioView.description: One declared scenario, rendered for display. The variant is chosen by `kind`: a fixture-backed scenario carries its file, a resolver-backed one carries its source, and either becomes `error` when the file cannot be read or parsed.

label.description: Friendly name — the fixture's or resolver's description, falling back to the slug.

summary.description: Secondary line, present only when the scenario declares a non-empty summary.

isDefault.description: True for the scenario whose slug is `default`.

json.description: The whole fixture file — status, headers, and body — as pretty-printed JSON.

html.description: Syntax-highlighted markup for the fixture body. Presentation data; read `json` instead.
Syntax-highlighted markup for `code`. Presentation data; read `code` instead.

ScenarioViewError.title: ScenarioViewError
ScenarioViewError.description: The scenario is declared, but its file could not be read or parsed.

message.description: What went wrong while reading the scenario's file.

GlobalMockScenario.title: GlobalMockScenario
GlobalMockScenario.description: A stored global override, with the timestamps the server keeps for it.

scenario.description: The scenario key in force: a declared scenario, or `real` for passthrough.

GlobalMockSelection.title: GlobalMockSelection
GlobalMockSelection.description: The selection a successful `PUT` put in force. Timestamps are not echoed — read them back with `GET /ui/api/global-mocks`.

scenario.description: A scenario declared on the endpoint, or `real` for passthrough.

ScenarioSelection.title: ScenarioSelection
ScenarioSelection.description: What a profile serves for one endpoint: a single scenario key, or an ordered sequence served call-by-call that sticks on its last step once exhausted.

displayName.description: Friendly label, present only once one has been set.

endpointScenarios.description: Endpoint name → selection, holding only endpoints this profile pins. Endpoints left on the implicit scenario are absent, so an empty object means the profile pins nothing.

displayName.description: Friendly label. A blank string, or a value that is not a string, is ignored and leaves any stored name unchanged.

endpointScenarios.description: Endpoint name → selection. Replaces the stored map wholesale; omit it, or send `{}`, to clear every selection.

endpoint.description: Reset only this endpoint's progress. Omit it — or omit the body entirely — to reset the whole profile.

version.description: The running build's package version, or `0.0.0-dev` for a build that was not stamped.

sha.description: The running build's full git SHA, or `unknown` for a build that was not stamped.

error.description: Why the ping failed — a driver message, or a timeout notice when the check outran its 3-second bound. Unlike every other failure on this API, this body is not the `Error` envelope.

ValidationFilter.title: ValidationFilter
ValidationFilter.description: Schema-validation states a log listing can be narrowed to.

ValidationResult.title: ValidationResult
ValidationResult.description: A schema check's outcome for one side of the exchange. The field is absent when that side was never checked — no schema, or the request never reached the check — which is a distinct state from `ok`.

path.description: Where the problem is. A body issue is a JSON pointer into that body, or `/` for the body itself. A parameter issue is `<location>/<name>` — `query/limit`, `header/x-tenant` — with a JSON pointer appended when the failure is inside a structured parameter value.

ValidationIssues.title: ValidationIssues
ValidationIssues.description: What failed on one side of the exchange. Bounded so a pathological body cannot inflate the entry.

list.description: The first few issues. Carried by the single-entry fetch; projected away in list summaries, which keep only `total`.

total.description: How many issues there were in all, including any beyond `list`.

LogTrace.title: LogTrace
LogTrace.description: How the server decided what to serve. Every field is optional: an entry carries only the steps its request actually took, and an admin entry carries only the admin fields.

profileResolution.description: How the caller's profile ID was found.

selector.description: The selector expression that produced the ID.

via.description: `direct` when the selector read the ID out of the request; otherwise the captured key mapping it was looked up through.

scenario.description: The scenario key that was served.

sequence.description: Position within a scenario sequence, when one was in play.

of.description: How many steps the sequence has.

served.description: How many calls the sequence has served in total — it keeps counting past the last step.

resolver.description: Present when a resolver-backed scenario ran.

returned.description: The scenario it decided to serve.

placeholders.description: Placeholder expression → the value it rendered to.

validation.description: Schema-check outcomes. Absent entirely when no check ran on either side.

issues.description: What went wrong, per side, for a side that is `failed` or `drift_warning`. A sibling of the flags rather than a shape wrapped around them, so entries written before this field existed still read cleanly.

delayMs.description: Injected response delay, when a fixture declared one. Already folded into the entry's `durationMs`; recorded here so injected latency is distinguishable from real work.

upstream.description: Present when the request was proxied to the real upstream.

adminAction.description: Set on `kind: "admin"` entries only: which control action was taken.

adminEndpoint.description: Set on `kind: "admin"` entries only: the endpoint a `progress_reset` was scoped to, absent for a whole-profile reset.

headers.description: Lowercased header names → values. An `authorization` header is stored as `[REDACTED]`.

body.description: The captured body: parsed JSON when the payload parsed as JSON, the raw text when it did not, and `null` when there was no body. Any JSON type, `null` included.

truncated.description: True when the body was cut to the capture limit, leaving `body` a raw string.

status.description: The status the server answered with.

LogEntryCommon.title: LogEntryCommon
LogEntryCommon.description: The fields a full entry and a list summary share.

logId.description: This entry's ID, also returned to the caller as the `x-mock-log-id` response header.

traceId.description: The caller's distributed-trace ID, when the request carried one: 32 lowercase hex from `traceparent`, or an `x-request-id` verbatim. Absent for untraced requests, and never present on admin entries.

durationMs.description: How long the request took end to end, including any injected delay. Absent on admin entries.

kind.description: `request` for a handled mock call; `admin` for a control action taken through this API or the dashboard.

profileId.description: The profile the call resolved to, when it resolved to one.

method.description: The incoming HTTP method. Absent on admin entries.

path.description: The incoming path. Absent on admin entries.

query.description: The incoming query string including its leading `?`, or an empty string when there was none. Absent on admin entries.

LogEntry.title: LogEntry
LogEntry.description: One recorded request, with everything the server captured for it.

LogSummary.title: LogSummary
LogSummary.description: A list row: a `LogEntry` without the captured payloads. The response keeps its status only, and each `trace.validation.issues` side keeps `total` without `list` — fetch the entry by ID for the rest.

LogBodyHtml.title: LogBodyHtml
LogBodyHtml.description: Syntax-highlighted markup for the entry's bodies, built for the dashboard. A side is absent when that body is missing, or was stored as a raw string rather than structured JSON.
